analysis.title: GS Quek - Weekend Thoughts 42/53 Tech positioning updates 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: Hot CPI revived debate on Fed hike risk, though the author expects October to be a hold. CXMT breakthrough claims triggered a sell-off in Korean memory names that spilled over to the global tech supply chain.

Weaker sentiment put AI capex sustainability, ROIC outcomes and funding requirements back in focus. Geopolitical tension and higher oil reinforced a negative feedback loop between rates, funding costs and global growth.
US economists raised 3Q26 tracking GDP by 20bps to 3.3% on industrial production strength.

European equities rose 2% on the week, a 4ppt outperformance vs SPX, the largest in more than a year, as AI/Momentum rotation played out. NIFTY rose 2.8% on the week. The author continues to pound the table on India private banks.
In the US, rotation went to defensives including Healthcare and Staples as markets broadened out. SPW closed the week +48bps.

This week's % net selling grossing in Global Tech was the largest on record. GS Prime book is underweight Tech vs MSCI World by -8.4%, in the 23rd/29th percentile on 1-year/5-year look back. Net allocation is in the 48th percentile on 1-year look back.

Cumulative selling over Oct 8-15 in the Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI) was roughly on par with the late-July episode and the largest since Mar '22. Positioning is roughly 6/10 on length and materially cleaner than Jun/July.
Unlike the July unwind, which felt largely technical, this episode has opened a real debate on fundamentals across rates/credit, earnings and ROIC.
Asia Tech is 18% of Global Net MV, vs a 27% June peak and 10% at the start of the year. North Asia bore the brunt of the risk-off move.
GS was net seller of $7.8bn in Asia this week: Taiwan -$2.75bn, China -$2.1bn, Japan -$1.9bn, Korea -$700m. Australia and India caught a bid.
Taiwan saw its largest net FII selling in history on 15 Oct and ended the week at -$19.2bn. Taiwan net allocations are still peakish and HF positioning in Taiwan is closer to the highs.

Korea positioning is cleaner. FIIs have sold $110bn+ since May. Net allocations sit in the 30th percentile vs the past 12 months but the 85th percentile on a 5-year look back. The Taiwan-vs-Korea selling divergence is one to watch next week.
FII ownership in Korea Semis is -2.5 SD below longer-term history. Leveraged ETF AUM fell from a $53bn peak to $15bn, or 1.3% of free float.

KOSPI fell more than 20% over eight trading days, a decline previously seen only during the Asian Financial Crisis, the Global Financial Crisis and COVID-19. The author says history suggests risk/reward looks very favorable and a tactical bounce looks due.

On CXMT's '4F2' architecture, the author thinks markets may have overestimated CXMT's ability to close the technology gap. 4F2 uses smaller, more complex and costlier memory cells, and CXMT still faces customer qualification, high-yield mass production and advanced nodes without direct EUV access.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is materially cleaner than Jun/July (about 6/10 on length), Korea FII ownership is at -2.5 SD and leveraged ETF AUM has fallen to $15bn. KOSPI's 20%+ drop has historically been followed by favorable risk/reward, pointing to a tactical bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: The episode has opened a real debate on fundamentals across rates/credit, earnings and ROIC, unlike the largely technical July unwind. Taiwan positioning is still peakish and Taiwan selling is at a record.

theme_stances.key_argument: KOSPI's 20%+ fall in eight sessions has only been matched in major crises, and history suggests favorable risk/reward from here.
